generator.model: claude-opus-5[1m] (Claude Code, Stage B; v0.1.1 replacement pass)

notes:
Supersedes v0.1-candidates, which stays on disk unchanged. One record differs: cv-0110 ("what tick size should i round hyperliquid prices to") was dropped at selection time and cv-0141 ("im deriving pancakeswap v3 pool addresses offline...") took its place, so the unanswerable slice is still 17 and the total is still 140. The other 139 records are carried over byte-for-byte: same ids, same field values, no renumbering. cv-0110 was dropped for two reasons. It was mislabelled: hyperliquid price rounding IS documented -- tickSize has zero occurrences in hyperliquid chunks, but szDecimals/nSigFigs/"significant figures" appear in 29 of them, so the question is answerable and the answer is a vocabulary correction, which is exactly what cv-0101 already tests as an adversarial item. And it duplicated cv-0101 at 0.926 cosine, above the 0.92 near-duplicate threshold this project uses. The replacement was chosen on a different venue and a different theme, and its gap was proven before the question was written: across pancakeswap chunks, CREATE2, keccak, salt, bytecode, encodePacked, deployer and getPool all return zero, and every spelling of the constant (init code hash / INIT_CODE_HASH / initCodeHash / init_code / POOL_INIT / creation code / bytecode hash) returns zero anywhere outside uniswap. The near-miss material is real: pancakeswap publishes the PancakeV3Factory address and a code comment naming computePoolAddress(), and uniswap publishes a complete CREATE2 recipe with a literal keccak256(init_code) -- for uniswap v2, the wrong protocol version and the wrong fork, so a retriever that answers confidently answers with the wrong constant.

Carried over from v0.1-candidates: candidate pool, unlabelled and unfiltered, input to human selection and not an evaluation set. Composition follows evals/METHODOLOGY.md, scaled from the 120 questions decided there to 140 and widened from five categories to the eight the schema defines. The methodology's five-way split (fact 35% / comparison 20% / multihop 12% / adversarial 18% / unanswerable 15%) is preserved in relative terms over the 121 questions in those five categories (fact 34.7% / comparison 19.8% / multihop 11.6% / adversarial 19.8% / unanswerable 14.0%); the remaining 19 slots go to the three categories the methodology did not name -- ambiguous (6), version_sensitive (7) and noisy (6) -- each above the five-question floor the validator enforces for a breakdown row. Adversarial items draw on the T1-T13 trap list in METHODOLOGY.md section 8. Because that section established that Uniswap/PancakeSwap duplication is conceptual rather than lexical (zero PancakeSwap chunks above 0.7 TF-IDF cosine to any Uniswap chunk), the fork traps here turn on shared concepts and diverging values -- fee tiers, Permit2 spender, router revert semantics -- not on copied wording. The corpus's genuine lexical duplication is intra-Binance (mainnet/testnet/Demo Mode), and it is used for both adversarial and version_sensitive items. Every answerable question was grepped against chunks.jsonl before it was written, and every unanswerable one was checked for supporting hits -- a check cv-0110 passed only because it was run against a single spelling (tickSize) and not against the vendor's own vocabulary (szDecimals, nSigFigs). That is the failure this version corrects. source_chunk_ids are provenance only and are NOT gold labels: they record where a question came from and let the annotator notice when the candidate pool fails to surface it. gold_chunk_ids and reference_answer are empty by design at this version.
